what: policy.default.deny_bash was applied to the main session as well as to sub-agents, denying the orchestrator git.
root_cause: The default block is documented as 'applies to any sub-agent identity not named below', but the code read it for every identity including the absent-identity case that means the main session.
prevention: When a policy has a default block scoped to one class of identity, write a test asserting the OTHER class is unaffected. test_hooks.py::test_main_session_may_run_git is that test.

what: A config-registry lint exempted keys by top-level segment only, so nested structural keys (analyze.taxonomy, ingest.roots) were reported as unregistered tunables.
root_cause: Exemption matched the first dotted segment rather than any segment, so an exempt name nested one level down never matched.
prevention: For dotted-path matching, decide explicitly whether the rule is prefix, suffix or any-segment, and test one nested case. Never leave it implicit.

what: Docstrings asserted safety properties ('tolerance is load-bearing', 'an unknown field can never leak', 'gates fail closed, always') that the code beneath them did not deliver.
root_cause: The prose was written from the design intent rather than from the implementation, and the tests were written to confirm that prose rather than to attack it.
prevention: For every claimed invariant, write the test that tries to BREAK it before writing the sentence that asserts it. If the attack is not in the suite, delete the claim from the docstring.

what: Two tools implemented the same rollup schema from separate specs and drifted (tokens vs totals), so every console token figure silently read zero while both test suites stayed green.
root_cause: Each agent was given the schema in prose in its own prompt; nothing made the producer and the consumer agree on one artifact.
prevention: Any data shape crossing a tool boundary gets a named CONTRACT constant in the producer plus a round-trip test in test_contracts.py that asserts the consumer surfaces the producer's numbers. Never re-specify a schema in two prompts.

what: A payload passed to a hook through an environment variable silently disabled the hook above 128KB.
root_cause: MAX_ARG_STRLEN caps a single env string; execve then fails, the script never runs, and a hook that emits no decision is read as allow.
prevention: Never pass tool payloads through the environment. Use a temp file, capture the child's exit status, and make a non-zero status fail closed for protected paths.

what: The bash denylist matched 'git' as a bare word anywhere, so any path under a folder named git/GIT (including this machine's ~/Documents/GIT/) made ls/cp/python3 read as running git.
root_cause: The test suite covered the adjacent false-positive class (gitleaks, mygit: word-boundary neighbors) and missed the path-segment class (/GIT/), so the rule looked tested while a whole class was uncovered.
prevention: When testing a text-matching rule, enumerate the CLASSES of false positive (word-inside-word, path segment, quoted mention, flag argument) and write one test per class, not one test per example.

what: Theme tokens landed in only one of the two dark blocks, twice in one day (--heading during the brand pass, --edge-* during the map recolor); the second block has different indentation so naive replaces hit once and report success.
root_cause: The template defines dark values in two places (media query and data-theme) with different indent; a single string-replace cannot see that it missed one.
prevention: Patch theme tokens with a script that counts occurrences and asserts count==2 before replacing, as the edge recolor finally did. A count of 1 is a failure, not a partial success.

what: Fixed-width README buttons passed a 900px local screenshot check but wrapped on GitHub's real container; the defect shipped and the maintainer caught it visually.
root_cause: The local render harness assumed a container width instead of matching the target surface's real one; a passing screenshot at the wrong width is false confidence.
prevention: Prefer percentage widths for README-embedded assets (they cannot wrap). When fixed pixels are unavoidable, render the local check at or below 830px content width and treat the target surface's real container as the spec, not the local guess.

what: The policy gate's protected-tree ring compared a platform-native relative path against posix-form prefixes, so on Windows every prefix test missed and the gate allowed sub-agent writes to the hooks, tools and configs that govern it.
root_cause: The prefix literals were written in posix form while the compared value came from str(Path) - correct on the development platform, silently inverted on the other one. The suite encoded the same assumption, so it went green where the gate was open.
prevention: In any gate, build a path for prefix matching with Path.as_posix() and test containment with os.path.normcase, never with str() or a bare relative_to; and run the full suite on each OS the system claims to support before tagging a release.

what: The PreToolUse matcher enumerated tool names (Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash) and never listed PowerShell, so on Windows an entire shell lane bypassed every ring the gate defends.
root_cause: A gate keyed to an enumerated list of harness tool names goes stale the moment the harness gains a lane; nothing in the suite asserted that the enumeration covers all shells that can mutate files.
prevention: When a gate enumerates harness tool names, keep one test per SHELL LANE (bash and PowerShell today) asserting the same denial through each. A lane with no test is a lane with no gate.

what: consolectl's write-gate compared the payload rather than the rendered page, so a template edit with an unchanged payload never reached the output while the generator ledger recorded it as fresh.
root_cause: The gate compared an INPUT to the render instead of the artifact it actually writes, which makes 'unchanged' mean something narrower than the file on disk.
prevention: A build write-gate compares the full artifact it writes, masking only the volatile fields it can name; never a subset of the inputs.
